key_insight: Halide ordering in mixed perovskites strongly reshapes phase stability, shifting structural transition temperatures by up to 100 K and explaining the non-linear composition dependence seen in CsPbBr3yI3-3y.
engineering_relevance: Controlling halide and A-site composition could improve thermal stability and phase predictability in perovskite solar cells, LEDs, and photodetectors.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for mixed halide perovskites.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample configurational and vibrational effects.
Mapped miscibility gaps and halide ordering across Br-Cl, Br-I, and Cl-I systems over 200–500 K.
evidence_signal: The study combines DFT-trained MLIPs with large-scale simulations and reports composition- and temperature-dependent miscibility gaps plus ordering-driven shifts in phase boundaries, including agreement with experimentally observed non-linear trends.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the fidelity of the trained MLIP and the specific Cs/Rb–Pb–halide composition space studied, so transfer to other perovskite chemistries may require revalidation.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
